It is the REGIONAL norm — e& (du's own duopoly counterparty), stc and Mobily all publish the subscriber split with a single blended ARPU, exactly as du does; Ooredoo is the sole Gulf exception. ACCESS CAVEAT, logged not papered over: investors.du.ae is intermittent from this environment (HTTP 200 on a direct request during this session, HTTP 503 on every attempt in a parallel verification pass), so the deck-level negative rests on the documents captured in this study's own first-hand extract of the Q2-2026 presentation rather than on a fresh re-read. g_term_real.source: Terminal REAL growth of ZERO, the house default for a real rate nobody has quantified. Real growth is now CHARGED for the capital it consumes, which this model's own forecast prices at AED 10,430mn per unit of real growth, so half a point of it is worth AED 52mn a year for ever. Assuming it away is the conservative reading and the sensitivity publishes the alternative rather than burying it

The policy note gives RANGES per class (buildings 10-25, plant and equipment 3-25, furniture and fixtures 3-5, motor vehicles 4-5, software 5-10) and no weighting, so no single figure can be read off it. sov_spread_market_observed.source: [KEY RENAMED 03-Sep-2026] This entry was keyed "sov_spread_rating", which said the OPPOSITE of its own source: the 17-Aug-2026 switch of primary basis swapped which construction was adopted and left the key names behind. The arithmetic and the delivered document were both correct throughout (rf* strips 4bp and the adopted ERP is the market basis, so country risk enters exactly once); only the key lied, and a key is what any other tool reads. PRIMARY BASIS (changed 17-Aug-2026): UAE sovereign default spread 4bp, MARKET-OBSERVED on the very instrument this model uses as its risk-free rate. The UAE MoF/WAM auction release records the January-2031 AED T-Bond pricing at 4.48% at a 4bp spread above the comparable US Treasury (read from the release, not quoted verbatim - the sentence is malformed in the original). The prior edition netted Damodaran's RATING-based 42bp instead, which drove rf* to 4.06% - roughly 26bp BELOW the matched-tenor US Treasury. A synthetic default-free dirham rate cannot sit below the default-free dollar rate under a hard peg, and that no-arbitrage test is now asserted in code. The rating basis (42bp with the 4.87% ERP, Ke 6.44%) is retained and published as the alternative construction per the both-bases rule; it is NOT averaged in. Note a floor applied to the rating basis was considered and REJECTED as incoherent: it would net a market spread while adding back a rating-based country premium, the exact same-basis violation the method exists to prevent

erp_market_basis.source: [KEY RENAMED 03-Sep-2026] This entry was keyed "erp_rating", which said the OPPOSITE of its own source: the 17-Aug-2026 switch of primary basis swapped which construction was adopted and left the key names behind. The arithmetic and the delivered document were both correct throughout (rf* strips 4bp and the adopted ERP is the market basis, so country risk enters exactly once); only the key lied, and a key is what any other tool reads. Paired with the 4bp netting above so the same basis is stripped as is added back. ALTERNATIVE PUBLISHED: the rating basis, 4.87% = 4.23% + 0.64% CRP (Aa2), paired with the 42bp netting -> Ke 6.44%. assert_log: DU — ASSERT / derivation log (built on audited FY23-25 + reviewed Q1/H1-2026 filings)

[Historical income statement] FY2025 EBITDA 7,338 is PRINTED on the face ('operating profit before depreciation and amortization', IFRS 18); FY2024 comparative likewise (6,470). FY2023 predates IFRS 18 and prints no such line — the 5,800 carried here is DERIVED from audited components and flagged. Margins: FY23 42.5%, FY24 44.2%, FY25 46.1%; H1-2026 ACTUAL 49.2%.

[Fiscal regime] combined royalty+tax take: FY2023 53.1% (OLD regime: 15% of regulated revenue + 30% of regulated profit), FY2024 42.2%, FY2025 43.6% (CURRENT regime: 38% royalty + 9% CT, legislated 2024-2026 only). The post-2026 regime is THE CONTESTED JUDGEMENT — both framings are computed and published side by side.

[Working capital, audited, royalty-accrual-adjusted] FY23 -965 (-7.1% of revenue), FY24 -1,220 (-8.3%), FY25 -1,062 (-6.7%) — structurally NEGATIVE, the classic prepaid/deferred-revenue telecom shape: customers and payables fund the operation. Cycle: DSO 51d (FY23 60d), payables 85d of revenue, inventory 5d of direct costs. The forecast holds the FY2025 component days constant, so NWC stays -6.7% of revenue and GROWTH RELEASES cash rather than absorbing it.

[Balance sheet] ZERO drawn borrowings in every year studied (Note 4.2 prints Total borrowings '–'); cash + term deposits: FY23 1,937, FY24 2,283, FY25 2,250. Lease liabilities (the only debt-like item): FY23 2,105 -> FY25 1,939. Net cash AFTER leases at FY2025: +311.
[Segment contribution margins FY24] mobile 60.9%, fixed 84.6%, wholesale 88.0%, ict 20.8%
[Segment contribution margins FY25] mobile 60.8%, fixed 85.8%, wholesale 86.4%, ict 19.4%

[Unit-build reconciliation, FY2025] avg mobile base 9,310k x ARPU AED 63.3 x 12 = 7,072 vs disclosed mobile segment revenue 7,075 (-0.0%) — the subscribers-x-ARPU frame reproduces the audited segment to within a percent.
[Mobile mix, disclosed] postpaid share of the base 20.2% (Q4-2024) -> 20.4% (Q4-2025) -> 22.1% (Q2-2026). The Q2-2026 jump is not postpaid strength alone: prepaid fell -499k while postpaid rose +74k.

[Is a prepaid/postpaid split IDENTIFIED? — NO. Tested across every quarter pair, not one] du publishes the base split every quarter but only ONE blended ARPU, so a two-leg build needs two unknowns per period against one disclosed equation. The mix DID move, which in principle pins the ratio between the legs if both are constant — so solve for it on all 21 available quarter pairs. The implied postpaid/prepaid ARPU ratio ranges -45.2x to 16.8x. 9 of 21 pairs imply a NEGATIVE ratio and 2 imply a postpaid subscriber worth LESS than a prepaid one — both impossible. Only 5 sit inside the 2.9x-7.2x band observed at the one Gulf operator that discloses both legs. An estimator that swings from -45x to 17x depending on which two quarters you pick is not identifying anything. THE SPLIT IS THEREFORE NOT BUILT: the build stays on the blended figure, which is the finest level du sources, and the gap is flagged rather than filled with an imported ratio. Note the arithmetic is also mix-preserving — at unchanged mix EVERY ratio in the peer band reproduces the same blended ARPU and the same audited revenue — so a split would add an unsourced driver and no information.

[What the flat blended ARPU is actually hiding — mix decomposition] at a 3.0x postpaid/prepaid ratio, the +1.83pp mix shift alone would have lifted blended ARPU +2.61%. The company printed +0.16%. So each leg's own ARPU eroded about -2.39% over the same span, and the flat headline is a COINCIDENCE of two offsetting forces, not stability. THE RISK THIS CREATES: the mix shift came from a one-off collapse in low-value visitor prepaid SIMs, and the subscriber path in this study assumes prepaid RECOVERS. A recovering prepaid base pushes the postpaid share back DOWN, which removes the tailwind and leaves the underlying leg erosion exposed. Priced below as the mix-exhaustion scenario, and carried into the caveats.

[Direct-cost unit rates, from du's own filings] AED per subscriber per month unless shown as a rate. FY24: mobile interconnect 18.24 + commission 5.69 + devices 0.52 = 24.45; fixed capacity 79.71; wholesale 11.97%; ICT 79.25% | FY25: mobile interconnect 17.40 + commission 6.14 + devices 1.26 = 24.81; fixed capacity 73.14; wholesale 13.58%; ICT 80.61% | H125: mobile interconnect 17.54 + commission 6.12 + devices 1.40 = 25.06; fixed capacity 75.29; wholesale 13.94%; ICT 80.77% | H126: mobile interconnect 16.81 + commission 6.31 + devices 0.96 = 24.08; fixed capacity 68.35; wholesale 15.58%; ICT 78.48%

[Like-for-like half-year direction] mobile interconnect 17.54 -> 16.81 (-4.1%); commission 6.12 -> 6.31 (+3.0%); fixed capacity 75.29 -> 68.35 (-9.2%). Only the first two carry a named mechanism and a drift; the rest are anchored on H1-2026 and held flat.

[Is the H1 rate a fair stand-in for H2? — H2-2025 actuals] mobile 25.01 vs H1-2025 25.06; fixed 71.33 vs 75.29; wholesale 13.22% vs 13.94%; ICT 80.47% vs 80.77%. Three of the four second-half rates came in CHEAPER than the first half, so carrying the H1-2026 rate into H2-2026 overstates cost rather than understating it.

[Contribution margin — now an OUTPUT of a costed unit build] mobile 62.2%->62.8% (audited FY2025 60.8%, H1-2026 actual 62.4%); fixed 87.3%->88.0% (audited FY2025 85.8%, H1-2026 actual 87.3%); wholesale 84.4%->84.4% (audited FY2025 86.4%, H1-2026 actual 84.4%); ict 21.5%->21.5% (audited FY2025 19.4%, H1-2026 actual 21.5%)

The retired input ignored six months of reviewed data in every segment.
[Revenue build] FY26E 16,593 (+4.3% vs guidance 4-6% revised 23-Jul-2026) -> FY30E 19,424. Segments FY26E: mobile 7,209, fixed 4,806, wholesale 2,548, ict 2,031

[Is the FY2026E margin too rich? — TEST IT ON THE IMPLIED SECOND HALF] the build's FY26E 47.8% sits above the company's guided 46-47%, so the claim to defend is the implied H2-2026 margin of 46.5%. H1 improved +2.1pp y/y (47.1% -> 49.2%); the implied H2 improves only +1.3pp y/y (45.2% -> 46.5%). The forecast therefore assumes the y/y margin gain roughly HALVES in the second half. The guided range is a full-year figure the company set in July against a first half that had already printed 49.2%; hitting the 46.5% midpoint would require an H2 margin of 43.9%, i.e. a y/y DETERIORATION of -1.3pp against an H1 that improved. That is a possible outcome and it is priced in the sensitivity, but it is not the central case the filings support.
[D&A roll-forward] FY26E 2,235 (2x reviewed H1-2026 actual = 2,266 — within 1.4%); PP&E 10,289 -> 12,432.

[WACC terminal] Ke 6.35%; Kd after tax 2.77%; weights 95%/5% -> 6.17%

[Terminal] life 16.70y derived; maintenance 3,047 against owned book charge 2,582; working-capital line -26 (a CREDIT — this company collects before it pays); terminal FCFF 3,358 = 86.7% of terminal profit; TV 82,050 against the retired 85,964 (-4.6%) at g 2.00% / WACC(term) 6.17%

Framing 2 (no re-rating: du's current multiple held into perpetuity): AED 13.89. Gap +2.68/share. Published side by side; never averaged.

[Post-2029 fiscal tail — no longer the contested judgement, du disclosed the 2027-2029 extension itself on 24-Jul-2026] Current regime (43.6% take): AED 16.58. Framing B (reversion to the pre-2024 construction, effective take 51.1% -> 50.9%): AED 14.74. Gap +1.84/share (-11%). Published side by side; never averaged.

[rf tenor gap, BOTH ALTERNATIVES PRICED] base rf 4.48% (Jan-2031 AED T-Bond, 30-Jul-2026) -> AED 16.58. LONGER, LOWER: the Feb-2033 AED Islamic Treasury Sukuk second tap at 4.13% (23-Apr-2026) -> WACC 6.06% -> AED 18.77 (+2.19/share, +13.2%). LONGER, HIGHER: the 10y peg-extrapolated 4.69% -> WACC 6.60% -> AED 16.44 (-0.14/share). The base sits BETWEEN the two, which is the point: there is no liquid 10-year AED point, so the tenor choice is a real range and it is published as one.

[The critique's rf, PRICED before it is judged] the Feb-2033 sukuk's DEBUT print 3.779% (22-Feb-2026) -> WACC 5.73% -> AED 20.59 (+4.01/share, +24.2%) — so the finding is MATERIAL and had to be re-derived, not waved away. It is nonetheless REJECTED on the evidence: the issuer's own second tap of the SAME instrument cleared 4.13% two months later, and the Jan-2031 T-Bond moved 3.90% -> 3.85% -> 4.30% -> 4.48% across the same window. A debut print 5.5 months before the anchor is not the rate that prevailed at the anchor.
[DCF scenarios] bear 10.57 / base 16.58 / bull 27.67 AED per share

[Relative lens] trailing P/E 17.7x, trailing EV/EBITDA 7.0x (du's own, computed from audited figures). Justified P/E 12.9x (Mobily, the closest structural analogue, from its own filings — NO peer median is claimed: only 2 of 6 peers survive as clean observations) x FY26E EPS 0.71 -> AED 8.90 at the anchor [bear 12x 8.24 / bull 18.5x 13.05]. [Normalised lens] mid-cycle margin 47.9% (FY2028E) on FY2026E revenue -> normalised EPS 0.71 x 12.9 = AED 8.92 at the anchor

[Book lens] justified P/B = (27% − 2.0%) / (6.35% − 2.0%) = 5.74x on BVPS 2.24 -> AED 12.76 at the anchor. A 27% sustainable ROE against a 6.4% cost of equity is what a licensed duopoly with negative working capital looks like; the multiple is high because the equity base is small, not because the claim is aggressive. Trailing ROE 29.0%.
[Synthesis] the cash-flow lens IS the central, AED 16.58; span 10.57 - 27.67; spot 11.36 (+46% to the central).

[Mix-exhaustion scenario, PRICED] if the postpaid mix tailwind exhausts and the blended ARPU path instead erodes at the per-leg rate the decomposition implies (-2.39%/yr), the DCF is AED 13.66 against the base 16.58 (-2.92/share, -17.6%). Grid across ARPU drift: -2.5% -> 13.53, -1.5% -> 14.72, +0.0% -> 16.58, +0.5% -> 17.22, +1.0% -> 17.86.

[CC7 PRICED — Expert 1's discounting horizon] as built AED 9.93 (net exponent -1.33 years). Horizon corrected to the anchor-consistent 2.40 years and nothing else: AED 9.89 (-0.04/share). But that version silently discards the dividends receivable between the anchor and FY2028, worth AED 1.64 in present value on a payout near 100%; adding them back gives AED 11.54 (+1.60/share vs as built, +9.7% of the central). VERDICT: the finding's PREMISE is correct and was under-priced by being left unpriced — the horizon really is a year short. Its CONCLUSION that the lens is overstated is wrong in sign once the omitted dividends are restored. Expert 1 is republished on the coherent construction.

[CC10 RESOLVED — the market-multiple family's weight] the finding said the weight scheme was a house judgement that moved the answer, and it was right. It was priced against the blend this study published at the time, AED 12.74: moving the freed 20% to the cash-flow lens gave AED 14.28 (+1.53/share) and to the book lens AED 13.51 (+0.77/share) — up to 1.53/share, not immaterial. VERDICT: RESOLVED, and not by re-tuning the weights. The scheme is gone: the cash-flow lens IS the central at AED 16.58 and the others are published beside it, so there is no weight left to re-set. The finding pointed at a free parameter nobody had tested and the answer was to remove it rather than to choose it better. The arithmetic above is kept as the record of what the retired construction did, and the blend itself is published unused.

[CC3 PRICED — revenue at the guidance midpoint] the build lands at +4.3% against du's guided 4-6%, so the midpoint +5.0% is +0.7pp above it, worth about AED 107mn of FY2026 revenue. Won on PRICE (blended ARPU 1.018x, no incremental unit cost or capex): AED 17.16 (+0.58/share). Won on VOLUME (+337k subscribers, carrying both unit cost and the capex it implies): AED 17.28 (+0.71/share). So the finding is worth AED +0.58 to +0.71 a share and is NOT immaterial.

[Why volume looks better here — the comparison was mis-specified, and the fix] calibrating both cases on FY2026 growth does NOT hold revenue constant, because H1-2026 is a reviewed ACTUAL: a subscriber shift can only move the second half of FY2026, so matching FY2026 needs a shift large enough to then apply to the WHOLE of FY2027-FY2030. Five-year revenue comes out 91,049 on price against 91,862 on volume (+0.89%) — the volume case simply sells more over the window. That is a timing artefact of the calibration, not evidence about attribution.

[CC3, attribution isolated on matched five-year revenue] +190k subscribers delivers the same 91,049 of five-year revenue as the price case. On PRICE: AED 17.16. On VOLUME: AED 16.98 (-0.18/share, -1.1%). NOW the expected ordering holds: identical revenue is worth less when it has to be bought with per-subscriber cost and the capex to carry the traffic. VERDICT on the finding: material, published as a range. The build stays below the midpoint because it is driven by disclosed subscriber and ARPU paths rather than reverse-engineered to a guidance number — but the reader is entitled to see what the midpoint is worth and that HOW it is won matters as much as whether it is.
